'''''Marsilea quadrifolia''''' is a herbaceous plant found naturally in central and southern Europe, Caucasia, western [[Siberia]], Afghanistan, south-west India, China, Japan, and Vietnam, though it is considered a weed in some parts of the United States, where it has been well established in the northeast for over 100 years.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nas.er.usgs.gov/taxgroup/plants/docs/marsilea/marsilea.html |title=Non-indigenous Aquatic species |access-date=2017-09-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120207204801/http://nas.er.usgs.gov/taxgroup/plants/docs/marsilea/marsilea.html |archive-date=2012-02-07 }}</ref> Its common names include '''four leaf clover''' and '''European waterclover''' (USA), even though it is not a species of [[clover]].

==Description==
Aquatic fern bearing 4 parted leaf resembling [[Four-leaf clover|'Four-leaf clover' (Trifolium)]]. Leaves floating in deep water or erect in shallow water or on land. Leaflets obdeltoid, to 3/4" long, glaucous, petioles to 8" long; [[Sporocarp (ferns)]] ellipsoid, to 3/16" long, dark brown, on stalks to 3/4" long, attached to base of petioles.{{Cn|date=May 2021}}

==Uses==
In some places it has been used as food for more than 3000 years. The plant is said to be [[anti-inflammatory]], [[diuretic]], [[depurative]], [[febrifuge]] and [[refrigerant]].<ref>[http://www.pfaf.org/database/plants.php?Marsilea+quadrifolia  Plants For a Future]</ref> It is also used to treat snakebite and applied to abscesses.{{Cn|date=May 2021}}

==Cultivation==
{{More citations needed section|date=May 2021}}
The plant prefers light (sandy) and medium (loamy) soils. It can grow in semi-shade (light woodland) or no shade. It requires moist or wet soil and can grow in water.<ref>[http://www.pfaf.org/database/plants.php?Marsilea+quadrifolia  Plants For a Future]</ref>

''Marsilea quadrifolia'' can be grown as a potted plant, either just with soil kept wet, or semi-submerged, with fronds emergent from the water, or fully submerged, with the fronds floating on the surface of the water.

In the [[aquarium]], water clover is grown fully submerged, usually in the foreground where it spreads by means of runners. It normally seems to be unfussy as to light and water conditions, and doesn't need a rich substrate.

Marsilea are very easy to germinate from their [[Sporocarp (ferns)|sporocarps]].  However, the sporocarps must be abraded, cracked, or have an edge sliced off before submerging them in water so that the water can penetrate to swell the tissues, and germination is infrared-light dependent.  Full sunlight is fine for this purpose.
